answer: Admission is priced in joules: a verifier called WattSeal reads a signed power trace from a certified meter bound to one seat and rejects any reading whose draw misses the declared workload, so one machine cannot claim a hundred seats. The penalty trigger is a shared meter collision: two seats on one meter ID lose both bonds and operator escrow freezes. A meter costs eighteen dollars and each seat draws sixty watts, near seven dollars monthly, so N fakes cost N times twenty five dollars, a bill that climbs like a spiral with no flat tundra to hide in and no cheap timber to burn twice.
